answer.reason: Most verses use Hamath only as a northern boundary marker, but two state events that happened to it: its recovery for Israel and the store cities Solomon built there.

clauses.english: was recovered for Israel by Jeroboam son of Joash
clauses.quote: he recovered Damascus, and Hamath, which belonged to Judah, for Israel

clauses.english: had store cities built in it by Solomon
clauses.quote: all the store cities, which he built in Hamath

doubts: Left out the many verses that use 'the entering in of Hamath' only as a boundary.
Left out Riblah in the land of Hamath (2KI 23:33, 2KI 25:21, JER 39:5), since those events happened at Riblah.
Toi king of Hamath (2SA 8:9, 1CH 18:9) is a deed of the king, not of the place.
Hamathzobah (2CH 8:3) may be a different place, so it is not used.
The Assyrian taunts about Hamath's gods (2KI 18:34, 2KI 19:13) are rhetorical questions and do not state an event.
